message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to say "See you next year!" to this teacher who's getting let go. Let me start by understanding the situation better. First, there's this teacher, R, who just started at my school this year. From the beginning, R tried to impose his own teaching and grading methods, which were very different from what we've ever experienced. Even if his methods were wrong and people pointed that out, we were still expected to follow them. That sounds pretty frustrating because as students, we want our teachers to be open to feedback and willing to adapt, right? Also, R took off points for scratch work that he didn't like and tried to deduct as many points as possible on tests, quizzes, and homework. Every student he had was subjected to this, without exception. That seems really harsh and unfair. It's one thing to have strict grading, but when it's consistently applied in a way that seems punitive, it can really affect students' motivation and confidence. Moreover, R took forever to grade assignments. We took a test the week before spring break and didn't get it back for about six weeks. That's a long time, and it means students can't learn from their mistakes in a timely manner. Also, R refused to go over the test with anyone, which is another missed opportunity for learning and clarification. On top of that, R never offered help outside of the classroom and was hostile whenever asked for extra help. That's really problematic because part of being a teacher is being available to support students when they need it. If R was unwilling to provide that support, it made the learning environment even more challenging. The administration noticed these issues, and we were informed that R wasn't coming back next year. Understandably, we were all overjoyed about this news. After the announcement, R completely checked out. He wrote notes on the board, barely talked during class, and even went to Disneyland instead of attending one of the review days for exams. That seems like a lack of responsibility and commitment to his students. Now, yesterday, as I was walking out of R's classroom for the last time, I called over my shoulder, "See you next year!" My friends told me I'm the asshole for this, but I don't think so. Is it AITA (Ask If Truly Appropriate)? First, I need to consider the context. R was a teacher who was not performing well, was unfair in grading, and was generally unpleasant to students. The administration decided not to renew his contract, which was a relief for everyone. After that, R stopped putting effort into his teaching, which was disappointing. Saying "See you next year!" in this context could be interpreted in a couple of ways. On one hand, it's a casual goodbye, acknowledging that we won't see each other next year. On the other hand, given R's behavior and the administration's decision, it might come off as sarcastic or even mocking, implying that we're happy he's leaving. I need to think about the intent behind the statement. Was I trying to be friendly, or was there an underlying tone of sarcasm or disrespect? If it was meant to be friendly, then it's just a simple goodbye. However, given the context of R's poor performance and the administration's decision, it's easy to see how it could be perceived negatively. Also, considering that R had already checked out and was hostile, maybe there's a part of me that wanted to assert my feelings or get a reaction. But is that appropriate? As a student, it's important to maintain a certain level of respect, even if the teacher hasn't been the best role model. Another angle is the impact of the statement. If R heard it and felt disrespected, that could be problematic. However, if it was just a casual remark without any malice, maybe it's not that big of a deal. But since my friends are telling me I'm the asshole, it suggests that they perceive it negatively. I also need to reflect on whether this kind of remark is something I would do in a more positive or neutral situation. If a teacher was leaving under good circumstances, would I say the same thing? Probably not, because the context is different. So, the fact that R was leaving under negative circumstances influences how the statement is perceived. Additionally, I should consider the broader implications of how students interact with teachers, especially those who are struggling. While it's important to hold teachers accountable for their performance, it's also important to maintain a respectful and constructive relationship. Dismissive or mocking remarks, even if they're just a casual goodbye, can contribute to a negative environment. In summary, while the intent behind saying "See you next year!" might have been neutral, the context in which it was said makes it easy to interpret it negatively. Given that R was already struggling and the administration had decided not to renew his contract, the remark could be seen as disrespectful or mocking. Therefore, it might not have been the most appropriate thing to say, even if I didn't intend it that way. I also need to consider how I would feel if someone said something like that to me in a similar situation. If I were on the receiving end, would I feel disrespected? Probably, yes. So, that's another reason to think that it might not have been the best choice of words. Moreover, maintaining a respectful demeanor, even in difficult situations, is an important life skill. It shows maturity and the ability to handle conflicts gracefully. By keeping interactions respectful, it sets a positive example for others and contributes to a healthier overall environment. In conclusion, while the remark itself wasn't inherently malicious, the context and potential perception make it a bit problematic. It's something to be mindful of in the future, to ensure that interactions, especially with authority figures, are respectful and constructive.
